title: Boss: divide and conquer
summary: Helper functions and recursion working together.

steps.title: Module boss
body: For each recursive problem: write the base case first, then trust the smaller call. For each helper: give it one job and a name that says what it returns.

steps.title: Fast power
prompt: Write `long Power(long x, int n)` recursively for `n >= 0`, but faster than multiplying `n` times:
- if `n` is even, `x^n` is `half * half` where `half = x^(n/2)`
Compute `half` **once** and store it in a box; calling `Power(x, n / 2)` twice would throw away the speed-up.

forbid.message: Uses recursion, not loops or Math.Pow

hints: Three cases, in this order: `n == 0`, odd `n`, even `n`.
`long half = Power(x, n / 2); return half * half;`

steps.title: Palindrome, recursively
prompt: Write `bool IsPalindrome(string s)` recursively: a string is a palindrome if its first and last characters match **and** the middle (without them) is a palindrome. Strings of length 0 or 1 are palindromes.
hints: Base case first: length 0 or 1 is always a palindrome.
A mismatch at the ends is a guard clause that returns `false` straight away.

steps.title: Count the paths
prompt: A robot on a grid can only move **right** or **down**. Write `int Paths(int rows, int cols)` returning how many different routes take it from the top-left to the bottom-right of a `rows` by `cols` grid.
If either dimension is 1, there is exactly one route (a straight line). Otherwise every route starts by going right (leaving a `rows` by `cols - 1` grid) or down (leaving `rows - 1` by `cols`).
hints: Base case: a single row or a single column.
Add the two choices: `Paths(rows, cols - 1) + Paths(rows - 1, cols)`.

steps.title: Save codes
prompt: Old console games saved your progress as a short **password** you wrote down. Delve does the same: a code like `14KZRH` brings back the floor, your hit points and your purse.

The code is a number written in **base 32** with the digits `const string Digits32 = "0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ";` (no I, L, O or U, so nobody misreads them). Write, **recursively** for the two conversions:

1. **`static string ToBase32(int n)`** for `n >= 0`: like `DigitSum` peeling off `n % 10` and recursing on `n / 10`, the last digit is `Digits32[n % 32]` and the rest are `ToBase32(n / 32)`. `ToBase32(1000)` is `"Z8"`, `ToBase32(0)` is `"0"`.

2. **`static int FromBase32(string s)`**: the reverse. The value of `s` is the value of everything but its last digit, times 32, plus the last digit's position in `Digits32` (`Digits32.IndexOf(c)`). The empty string is 0.

3. **`static string SaveCode(int floor, int hp, int copper)`** (hp at most 99, copper at most 9999): pack `packed = (floor * 100 + hp) * 10000 + copper`, then the code is `ToBase32(packed)` followed by one **check digit**, `Digits32[packed % 31]`. `SaveCode(1, 20, 120)` is `"14KZRH"`.

4. **`static int[] LoadCode(string code)`**: upper-case it first. Return `{ floor, hp, copper }`, or an **empty array** when the code is shorter than 2 or longer than 7 characters, has a character that is not in `Digits32`, or its check digit is wrong.
starter: static string SaveCode(int floor, int hp, int copper)
solution: static string SaveCode(int floor, int hp, int copper)
template: Dojo.Eq("LoadCode(\"30rnq9\"): lower case is fine", new[] { 3, 17, 999 }, LoadCode("30rnq9"));
Dojo.Eq("a wrong check digit is refused", new int[0], LoadCode("14KZRJ"));
Dojo.Eq("a mistyped digit is refused", new int[0], LoadCode("14KZQH"));
Dojo.Eq("U is not a base-32 digit", new int[0], LoadCode("14UZRH"));

forbid.message: Every function starts with `static` (Delve keeps its pieces in one static class)

hints: ToBase32 mirrors DigitSum from Recursion, with 32 in place of 10: base case `n < 32` returns one digit as a string (`Digits32[n].ToString()`).
FromBase32: `s.Substring(0, s.Length - 1)` is everything but the last character.

LoadCode: check the length, then every character (`Digits32.IndexOf(c) < 0` means not a digit), then decode all but the last character and compare its check digit. Unpack with `/` and `%`: `packed / 1000000`, `packed / 10000 % 100`, `packed % 10000`.

build.title: Save codes
build.unlocks: Type save in Delve to get a code; type the code when Delve starts to carry on.
transform: // Your passing code from the code-dojo Programming fundamentals track.
